parsed.why: No criminal statute (2019 ban repealed 2020; 2024 constitution rejected re-criminalisation, added privacy), state harassment of LGBTQ groups absent. But no recognition, no protections, occasional modesty-charge misuse against gender-nonconforming people, common individual harassment, military rule, border practice undocumented.

Lawful since 1977, hate-crime law covering gender identity, documented social acceptance (travel guide, city centres, mayors), no criminalisation, no facility or custody exposure. Deductions: uneven anti-discrimination enforcement, under-reporting, anti-gender political hostility, documented search difficulties.

Colonial male-sodomy felonies still in force (up to 14 years) reaching trans women read as male, though prosecutions absent since 2013 in a thin record; no gender-identity protection, no recognition, traditional discrimination, custody and border practice undocumented. Extrapolated toward structural risk.

Enforced criminalisation (44 arrested, convictions), de facto ban on transition care and on being trans, police complicity and impunity in beatings and killings of gender-nonconforming people, no organising, no establishments, relocation officially harder for trans women. Severe state-tolerated targeting.

No sodomy law and hate-crime coverage, but national border regime refuses/targets mismatched documents (advisories by eight governments, detentions), bathroom bans in roughly half the states with one arrest and men's-ward custody, harmful inmate and immigration-detention practices.
